claim_verdicts.evidence: R2: §3 now adds 'no item moves into it from the column before'; still within the claim ('no new item is pulled into it until one leaves'). Glossary wip-limit: 'A cap on how many items can sit in one column at once'. The Kanban Guide (WebFetch summary): 'Kanban system members should refrain from selecting more than the number of work items into a given part of the workflow beyond the WIP control' and 'Ideally, the system would operate neither above nor below the agreed upon control.'

Unchanged since R1. git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:docs/team/kanban-board-example.md: line 8 'Đang làm (giới hạn 2) | Chờ review (giới hạn 2)'; lines 10-11 two items in Đang làm (Dev 3, Dev 2), one in Chờ review (Dev 1). Lines 16-20 'Dev 4 vừa xong một việc ... Trưởng nhóm chặn lại ... đi giúp một việc đang có sẵn ... Một cột đầy là tín hiệu tắc nghẽn'. Both code blocks re-checked verbatim in R2.

Unchanged in substance; R2 wording 'shows where work is stuck' replaces 'bottleneck'. The Kanban Guide (WebFetch summary): 'Controlling WIP helps flow and often improves the Kanban system members' collective focus, commitment, and collaboration.' Repo file line 19: 'Một cột đầy là tín hiệu tắc nghẽn'.

Unchanged since R1. Board lines 10-12: Đang làm 2/2, Chờ review 1/2. Step 2 -> Chờ review 0/2, Đang làm 2/2. Step 3 -> product page fix to Chờ review (line 34 'sang "Chờ review" khi pull request mở'), Chờ review 2/2, Đang làm 1/2. R2 suggested answer ('as the product page fix did in step 3') is consistent with this.

Kind opinion, stated with its mechanism in §6 ('because everyone's time is split across all of them'): if a person's time is divided across more open items, each item gets less of it and takes longer; this follows from the stated premise. The Kanban Guide (WebFetch summary) has no Little's Law or cycle-time sentence, only 'Controlling WIP helps flow', which points the same way. No throughput-per-week claim remains.

issues.text: Stated as a general rule, but The Kanban Guide's WIP control applies to 'a workflow from started to finished' or 'a given part of the workflow', not necessarily one column. Glossary and claim 1 define it per column, so this is only a wording tightening.
issues.quote: A **WIP limit** belongs to one column; on the Đơn Hàng team's board it is the number in brackets after the column name.
issues.fix: Replace with: "On the Đơn Hàng team's board, each **WIP limit** belongs to one column: it is the number in brackets after the column name."

issues.quote: Actually the limit is a rule, not a hint: the team treats a full column as closed, as the team lead does with Dev 4, and the number on the column shows everyone at once when the rule is broken.
issues.text: R1 fixed: 'a rule, not a hint' now clearly answers the 'suggestion' half. The 'not enforced by structure' half is still left unanswered; I infer the board does not block cards by itself, so part of the belief seems right, but the text does not say so.
issues.fix: Add a short clause after 'a rule, not a hint:', e.g. 'the board does not stop a card by itself;', so it is clear the mistake is calling it a suggestion.

issues.quote: you know Kanban moves each item through board columns as soon as it is ready, and that the team's board marks two columns `(giới hạn 2)`, which this lesson explains.
issues.text: R1 partly fixed: the bullet now says this lesson explains the mark, but still begins 'you know ... that the team's board marks two columns'. The prerequisite summary does not mention these marks, so I am told I know something I do not remember learning.
issues.fix: Split into two clauses: 'you know Kanban moves each item through board columns as soon as it is ready. The team's board marks two columns `(giới hạn 2)`; this lesson explains that mark.'
